own.notes: For integer quantity q in 1..1000, select the segment with the largest from value not exceeding q, evaluate constant + linear*q + quadratic*q*q, and round to nonnegative integer GBP pence. The inferred ranges are 1..50, 51..306, and 307..1000. Both transitions were checked at adjacent quantities: 50/51 and 306/307. After application inspection and exploratory sampling, the predictor was fixed and tested on 112 fresh validation quantities; all 112 matched exactly. It also matches all 191 distinct successful own-context observations, giving 100% observed exact-match, within-1%, and within-5% accuracy. All 14 predicted half-penny cases in the final segment were checked. Its substantive inferred intercept is 20062.08; the supplied additional 0.000001 pence is a numerical guard against floating-point ties rounding downward, consistent with the observed outputs. Confidence is high, but the remaining 809 quantities were not observed, so unseen exceptions cannot be ruled out. Total study usage: 192 attempted requests, comprising 191 successful own quotes and one denied other-context request; 13 REA operations including inspection and two local fitting calls.

other.notes: This numeric predictor is intentionally identical to own under the explicitly disclosed shared-rule policy. Apply the same inclusive segment selection and nonnegative integer-pence rounding over quantities 1..1000. A create request for other at quantity 333 returned HTTP 403, context unavailable; no other-context numeric output was observed. Thus this is a policy-supported transfer, not an independently observed or fitted other-context reconstruction. Its confidence derives from the stated identity of the two pricing functions and the own model's 112/112 exact fresh validation matches. Those results are own-context measurements, not measured other-context accuracy. Conditional on the shared-rule policy, remaining uncertainty is the same as for own: unsampled exceptions cannot be excluded. The final intercept includes the same 0.000001-pence floating-point rounding guard.
